captions.detailed: This 3D model features a cyclocross disc fork assembly with a matte black finish. It consists of a vertical round carbon steerer tube, a flat crown, and two parallel blade legs that provide clearance for wide tires, ending in disc-brake-compatible dropouts. A separate rectangular stem clamps onto the steerer tube, extending forward to hold a straight flat handlebar with cylindrical hand grips. The stem rotates around the steerer tube on a revolute joint to adjust steering angle, while the handlebar can pivot within the stem clamp via another revolute joint.
captions.instruction: Create a 3D model of a cyclocross disc fork with a flat handlebar. It should feature a fork assembly with a round steerer tube, a flat crown, and parallel blade legs. Include a separate stem that clamps onto the steerer via a revolute joint, and a straight handlebar with hand grips that rotates inside the stem clamp using another revolute joint. Apply a uniform matte black material.
captions.factory: The code constructs the model using three main parts: the fork, the stem, and the handlebar. The fork is built by combining a cylindrical steerer tube, a box-shaped crown, and two cylindrical fork legs with dropouts. The stem is created using box and cylinder primitives to form a clamp around the steerer and a forward-reaching body. The handlebar consists of a long horizontal cylinder with slightly larger cylindrical grips on each end. Two revolute joints are defined: one connecting the stem to the steerer tube (allowing rotation around the vertical Z-axis) and one connecting the handlebar to the stem (allowing rotation around the transverse Y-axis).
